question.text: In a trust-based AIF structure, the Trustee's role as distinct from the AMC/Investment Manager is PRIMARILY:

answer.text: Overall administration of trust matters, with investment functions vested in the Investment Manager
Making investment and divestment decisions on behalf of the fund
Day-to-day portfolio rebalancing and FX hedging execution
Appointing the external IC members without manager consent

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.7.2 (Fund Governance Structure), the AMC / Investment Manager handles all investment and divestment related decisions while the Trustee is responsible for the overall administration of trust matters. Investment functions and fiduciary obligations are split between the IMA and the trust deed. The Trap: Option A inverts the roles (that's the Manager's job). Option C is portfolio execution (Manager/Custodian). Option D is false — external IC members are appointed by the Manager with investor consent where required. Cross-Exam Context: Trust-based structure rules also tested in Ch 1/2 and in XIX-A (Cat I/II). Manager's Pro-Tip: Keep Manager and Trustee strictly separate in operations — avoid any joint employee or shared reporting line. Regulatory inspections target 'pseudo-independent' trustees and will re-classify them if lines are blurred.
